source.title: On the Implicit Bias of Adam
source.authors: Matias D. Cattaneo; J. Klusowski; Boris Shigida

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the paper and appendices; no material cutoff or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The study varies Adam hyperparameters and measures both a gradient statistic and test accuracy, reporting their association. This conceptually tests whether a measured property tracks generalization, though it does not use the magnitude-aware sharpness measure in V7.
record.gate_note: Theoretical derivations and cited comparisons with other optimizers are not this study's empirical results. Rows cover the reported full-batch Adam ResNet-50 CIFAR-10 sweeps in Figures 4 and 5, plus the analogous simple CNN and Vision Transformer sweeps in Figures 7–10. Test accuracies are reported in prose, while the plots supply no exact values.
record.test_reason: The study measures associations between Adam hyperparameters, perturbed gradient one-norm and test accuracy. It does not compare Adam with SGD, and its gradient statistic is not V7's magnitude-aware sharpness measure. Its own results therefore test none of V1–V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors derive hyperparameter- and training-stage-dependent implicit regularization or anti-regularization for Adam and RMSProp, and present preliminary Adam experiments consistent with stronger anti-regularization accompanying worse generalization. They propose a possible explanation for previously reported adaptive-optimizer disadvantages, without demonstrating an Adam–SGD performance difference themselves.
record.recipe_differences: The empirical method varies Adam hyperparameters during full-batch CIFAR-10 training and measures perturbed gradient one-norm and test accuracy; it does not test the listed optimizer comparisons or V7's magnitude-aware sharpness measure.
record.method_sensitivity: Test accuracy and perturbed one-norm vary with β and ρ in the tested sweeps; the authors restrict β and ρ to avoid divergence and reduce large spikes. Architecture also differs across the reported experiments, though no architecture comparison is quantified in the supplied prose.

fits_no_version.finding: Across selected full-batch Adam hyperparameter sweeps on CIFAR-10, increasing rho raises peak perturbed gradient one-norm and lowers maximal test accuracy; increasing beta gives the opposite pattern. The authors report these directions for ResNet-50, a simple CNN and SimpleViT.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within these Adam training settings, stronger predicted implicit anti-regularization is associated with worse held-out accuracy.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 235 (2024)
record.problems: The experiments use full-batch Adam on CIFAR-10 and do not compare Adam against SGD. The authors call the evidence preliminary and report averages across three or five initialization seeds without error bars or significance tests. Several numerical results are shown only in figures. They exclude the divergence regime and restrict β and ρ to reduce instability; the reported maximal test accuracies are after training to near-perfect training accuracy. The paper's measured perturbed gradient one-norm is not the magnitude-aware sharpness statistic in V7.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible results omitted. Figure 3 compares Adam trajectories with an ODE approximation, not a claim version; Figure 6 tracks perturbed one-norm over epochs without corresponding test-accuracy comparison. Cited optimizer generalization comparisons are prior work, not this study's results.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance compared with natural-label training.
Width-dependent test error beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Comparative held-out performance of adaptive methods and SGD under specified tuning budgets, including recovery interventions.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Effects of adding or removing dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation tolerance, its association with generalization gaps, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The theoretical connection is to a first-order approximation of non-adaptive infinity-norm sharpness, not V7's magnitude-aware measure. All row states are cannot_determine relative to the listed versions; the study's own directional findings remain reported. References to optimizer comparisons and batch-normalization methods do not constitute new tests of V4 or V5.

versions.untested_parts: Adam versus SGD or momentum SGD on benchmarks under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size comparisons and fixed-epoch budget effects.
Magnitude-aware sharpness perturbations and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures; the paper measures perturbed gradient one-norm, not sharpness.
